question: What happens when you take in more food energy (calories) than your body burns off?

options.A: Excess energy is stored primarily as fat
options.B: The body uses up its protein stores completely
options.C: Cellular chemical reactions stop entirely
options.D: Metabolic rate drops permanently to zero

explanation: Think of it like money: if you earn more than you spend, you save the extra! The body packs away extra calories as fat tissue to use for a rainy day.

question: How do advanced medical technologies generally impact healthcare supply?

options.A: They can improve efficiency and expand diagnostic capabilities
options.B: They automatically decrease the number of patients seeking care
options.C: They always reduce the total cost of operating a hospital ward
options.D: They eliminate the need for skilled nursing staff completely

explanation: Spot on! New tech helps hospitals run smoother and test patients faster, boosting what the facility can handle.

question: What factor most determines what kind of birth defect a teratogen will cause?

options.A: Whether the placenta is anterior or posterior
options.B: Total volume of amniotic fluid present
options.C: Gestational age at the time of exposure
options.D: The mother's blood type and Rhesus factor

explanation: Brilliant! Timing is everything because different organs develop at different weeks; exposure during organogenesis causes structural issues, while later exposure affects growth. You nailed it!

question: Which type of safety intervention is generally considered the most effective at preventing future errors?

options.A: Holding a 10-minute verbal lecture during morning shift handover
options.B: Strong system changes like automated hard-stops or redesigning equipment layouts
options.C: Asking staff to memorize a new policy document binder
options.D: Sending out a mandatory email warning staff to be more careful

explanation: Forced functions and system redesigns rely on technology or environment rather than human memory, making them much more reliable. [learn more](GST319_U6_T1#GST319_U6_T1_h8)

question: What is an essential nursing responsibility before synovial fluid aspiration begins?

options.A: Drain the joint fluid independently at the bedside
options.B: Administer a general anesthesia to the patient
options.C: Perform a full surgical repair of the joint
options.D: Verify that informed consent has been signed

explanation: Because arthrocentesis is an invasive procedure, the nurse must ensure the patient understands the risks and has signed consent. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T8#GNS222_U1_T8_h4)

question: What do we call an infectious disease that jumps naturally from animals to humans?

options.A: Nosocomial infection
options.B: Idiopathic disease
options.C: Opportunistic pathogen
options.D: Zoonosis

explanation: A zoonotic disease (or zoonosis) is an infection that normally lives in animals but can cross over to infect humans.

question: What is the main goal of studying 'human factors' in nursing?

options.A: Increasing the number of night shifts a nurse can work
options.B: Punishing nurses who make mistakes during medication rounds
options.C: Reducing the salary costs of hospital administrative staff
options.D: Matching clinical work systems to human strengths and limits

explanation: You've got this! Human factors simply looks at how we interact with our workplace so we can design safer, easier systems—instead of just blaming people when things go wrong.

question: What does it mean to put research results into 'context'?

options.A: Translating the research report into three different languages
options.B: Comparing new study findings with past literature and clinical realities
options.C: Destroying old textbooks so staff only read the newest articles
options.D: Increasing the hospital budget to match the research costs

explanation: Contextualization just means looking at how new findings fit alongside existing science and whether they make sense on a busy ward.

question: How can nurses use data collected from post-disaster surveys and feedback sessions?

options.A: To write legal documents for insurance claim investigations
options.B: To refine future educational programs and strengthen community resilience
options.C: To eliminate the need for future community training drills
options.D: To prove that no mistakes were made during the emergency response

explanation: Brilliant! Feedback highlights weak spots in our communication, helping us prepare much better for the next time.

question: Why is getting the family involved crucial for successful home health care?

options.A: Families are legally required to pay for all hospital expenses
options.B: Families replace the need for professional nursing assessments
options.C: Family members make all final medical diagnoses
options.D: Family members perform many daily care tasks between professional visits

explanation: Informal caregivers handle routines like feeding and giving medication reminders when you're not there. Partnering with them makes all the difference!

question: Which part of the chain of infection does contact tracing target the most?

options.A: Infectious agent mutation
options.B: Host genetic susceptibility
options.C: Reservoir sanitization
options.D: Mode of transmission

explanation: You've got this! By finding exposed contacts and keeping them away from others, we block the germ from moving from one person to another.

question: What does the vital infection control rule 'one needle, one syringe, one time' mean for your daily practice?

options.A: Injection equipment must be used for only one patient and never reused
options.B: Syringes can be reused if they are washed with soap and water
options.C: Multiple patients can share a medication vial if a new needle is attached
options.D: Nurses should change needles between patients but keep the same syringe

explanation: It's simple and non-negotiable: a fresh, sterile needle and syringe for every single patient, every single time. You've got this rule down!

question: Which of these is a biological factor that affects emotional health?

options.A: Monthly income and housing stability
options.B: Access to community parks and recreation
options.C: Cultural beliefs about mental illness
options.D: Genetic predispositions and neurochemistry

explanation: Biological factors are all about what's happening inside our bodies—like our genes, physical health, and brain chemistry.

question: What is the name of the medication commonly used to treat an unruptured ectopic pregnancy medically?

options.A: Progesterone
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Magnesium sulfate
options.D: Methotrexate

explanation: Methotrexate is a chemotherapy drug that stops rapid cell division, safely ending an early ectopic pregnancy without surgery. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T29#GNS216_U5_T29_h6)

question: What is the primary trigger for diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA)?

options.A: Consuming too much dietary protein in a single sitting
options.B: An allergic reaction to oral anti-diabetic medications
options.C: Severe lack of insulin forcing the body to break down fat rapidly
options.D: Sudden extreme physical exhaustion after heavy exercise

explanation: When insulin is severely lacking, the body burns fat too fast for fuel. This creates acidic waste products called ketones, leading to DKA. You're mastering advanced concepts!

question: Why is finding the root cause so important before choosing a health intervention?

options.A: It is a legal requirement set by the federal ministry of health
options.B: It stops community members from asking too many questions
options.C: It ensures you treat the real source of the issue rather than just the symptoms
options.D: It guarantees that funding will double for the project

explanation: Brilliant! Finding the root cause stops us from wasting energy on surface fixes while the real problem keeps hurting the community. Smart nursing thinking!

question: You need to add more water to a running steam generator. What is your very first step?

options.A: Ask the parent to hold the steam nozzle away
options.B: Pour cold water slowly while the unit is still boiling
options.C: Turn off and unplug the unit before adding water
options.D: Cover the hot metal parts with a dry towel first

explanation: Always power down and unplug first! This protects you from electrical shocks and nasty steam burns.

question: A grateful family tries to give you an expensive cash gift for your home care. What is the right response?

options.A: Accept the gift privately to avoid hurting the family's feelings
options.B: Divide the money evenly among all members of the healthcare team
options.C: Keep the money as a bonus for providing excellent home care
options.D: Politely decline the gift while explaining professional boundary policies

explanation: It's a kind gesture from the family, but accepting expensive gifts compromises your professional objectivity. Always decline with kindness and grace.

question: How do case studies mainly help nursing students build real-world competence?

options.A: By teaching them how to repair broken hospital equipment
options.B: By replacing all hospital ward practicals with computer games
options.C: By forcing them to memorize long lists of medical terminology
options.D: By challenging them to analyze real patient situations and plan care

explanation: Case studies bridge that gap between boring textbook theory and the actual ward by letting you think through real patient scenarios.

question: Which process completely wipes out ALL microbial life, including tough bacterial spores?

options.A: Colonization
options.B: Antisepsis
options.C: Sterilization
options.D: Disinfection

explanation: Sterilization is the highest level of cleaning. It doesn't just clean; it destroys even the toughest spores to keep surgical tools completely safe! [learn more](GST114_U1_T1#GST114_U1_T1_h5)

question: A nurse wants to understand the deep feelings and experiences of mothers going through postpartum depression. Which study style fits best?

options.A: A qualitative narrative exploration
options.B: A randomized controlled drug study
options.C: A quantitative retrospective chart review
options.D: A quantitative experimental trial

explanation: Brilliant! When you want to hear people's stories and feelings in their own words, qualitative research is your go-to choice. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T13#GNS217_U3_T13_h2)

question: What is the main hazard of leaving heavy oxygen cylinders unmounted inside an ambulance?

options.A: They make the ambulance engine consume more diesel fuel
options.B: They will automatically run out of medical oxygen faster
options.C: They can become dangerous projectiles during sudden braking
options.D: They interfere with the vehicle's internal electrical system

explanation: Sudden stops create massive forward momentum, turning loose heavy items into severe safety hazards for the crew and patient. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T9#GNS315_U3_T9_h2)

question: A partner stops someone from working and refuses to give them any money. What kind of abuse is this?

options.A: Psychological abuse
options.B: Economic abuse
options.C: Physical abuse
options.D: Systemic abuse

explanation: Spot on! Controlling finances creates total dependence, making it very hard for a victim to walk away.

question: Why must nurses know that a normal pregnant woman can have a high white blood cell count?

options.A: To determine the correct dose of routine iron supplements
options.B: To avoid misinterpreting a normal pregnancy change as a severe infection
options.C: To calculate the exact date when spontaneous labour will begin
options.D: To prove that the mother's immune system is completely shut down

explanation: Good nursing judgment! Knowing what is normal for pregnancy prevents us from panicking or treating a healthy mum for an infection she doesn't have.

question: Why is a patient during the incubation period often difficult to identify in the community?

options.A: They only transmit the disease through direct blood transfusions
options.B: They produce antibodies that instantly neutralize all clinical signs
options.C: They look and feel completely healthy despite harboring the pathogen
options.D: They actively isolate themselves before any laboratory test

explanation: Because clinical signs have not yet appeared, infected individuals appear well and go about daily life unaware. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T84#GNS214_U1_T84_h1)

question: Why is an unconscious patient who is still breathing placed in the recovery position?

options.A: To make it easier to start an intravenous line
options.B: To prevent the tongue from blocking the airway and allow drainage
options.C: To lower the patient's blood pressure safely
options.D: To prepare the patient for immediate surgery

explanation: You got it! This position keeps the airway safe by stopping the tongue from sliding back, and lets any saliva or vomit drain safely out of the mouth.

question: What is the main legal risk if a nurse forgets to document a medication right after giving it?

options.A: The hospital computer system will delete the patient file
options.B: The pharmacy will automatically double the next scheduled dose
options.C: The patient's insurance company will refuse to pay the bill
options.D: Legally, the medication is considered unadministered

explanation: In nursing law, if it isn't charted, it didn't happen! Always document promptly to protect your license and your patient.

question: A community nurse notices that an elderly client's primary caregiver looks extremely exhausted and frustrated. What is the best way to document this observation?

options.A: Record specific behavioral signs of fatigue in the caregiver and note the risk of burnout
options.B: Write that the family member is lazy and refuses to help the sick client
options.C: Document that the home environment is completely peaceful and supportive
options.D: Ignore the observation because the family member is not the official client

explanation: Documenting caregiver strain objectively helps the healthcare team plan interventions to support the family and protect the client. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h4)

question: What happens when vaccination rates drop significantly below the herd immunity threshold in a population?

options.A: The natural immunity of citizens automatically increases
options.B: Outbreaks of vaccine-preventable diseases become likely
options.C: Passive immunity replaces the need for community protection
options.D: Viruses instantly mutate into harmless strains

explanation: Falling below the threshold leaves too many susceptible hosts, allowing infectious diseases to spread easily and spark outbreaks. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T8#GNS313_U1_T8_h5)

question: Which of these duties is a key part of system accountability in a hospital?

options.A: Notifying the doctor immediately when vital signs drop
options.B: Providing adequate staffing levels and well-maintained equipment
options.C: Performing bedside patient identity checks before giving medication
options.D: Submitting an accurate incident report after an adverse event

explanation: Management's job is to supply safe tools and enough staff so nurses can provide great care.

question: Why can certain tastes instantly bring back strong emotional memories?

options.A: Because sensory fibers travel through the vagus nerve to the heart
options.B: Because taste information bypasses the thalamus entirely
options.C: Because gustatory signals project directly to the limbic system and amygdala
options.D: Because the cerebellum coordinates taste with voluntary movement

explanation: Taste pathways connect right into the brain's emotional centers (like the limbic system and amygdala), linking flavors to feelings and memories!

question: How do patriarchal family structures often impact women's reproductive health in Nigeria?

options.A: They eliminate all cultural barriers to hospital delivery
options.B: They require husbands to attend all antenatal checkups
options.C: They often restrict women's autonomy in making healthcare decisions
options.D: They automatically grant women full control over household finances

explanation: In homes where men hold all the decision-making power, a woman may need her husband's permission or money just to visit a clinic, which can dangerously delay her care.

question: Why do health programs often fail when they are imposed from the outside without community involvement?

options.A: They fail to match cultural realities and local priorities
options.B: Governments never allow outsiders to visit villages
options.C: Local health workers refuse to touch foreign supplies
options.D: They always cost too much money to run

explanation: Interventions that ignore local values and real community needs lack ownership and fail to gain public trust. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T4#GNS124_U4_T4_h1)

question: What is another common name for prenatal care?

options.A: Neonatal monitoring
options.B: Postpartum care
options.C: Gynecological screening
options.D: Antenatal care

explanation: Prenatal care is widely referred to as antenatal care, representing health services provided during the period of pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h1)

question: What is the medical term for dangerously high blood sugar?

options.A: Hypertension
options.B: Hypokalemia
options.C: Hyperglycemia
options.D: Hypoglycemia

explanation: Hyperglycemia just means too much glucose floating in the blood. You've got this! Keep building that nursing vocabulary.

question: What is the main difference between an early marriage and a forced marriage?

options.A: Forced marriage involves financial payment, while early marriage involves religious rites.
options.B: Forced marriage only happens to adults, while early marriage only happens to children.
options.C: Early marriage is legally recognized worldwide, whereas forced marriage is always illegal.
options.D: Early marriage is based on age, while forced marriage lacks free and full consent from at least one party.

explanation: Spot on! Early marriage focuses primarily on the person's young age, while forced marriage happens when someone is pushed into it without their true, free consent.

question: Why is tracking data over time with a wearable better than a single blood pressure check at the clinic?

options.A: It prevents nurses from having to manually record any vital signs
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for any laboratory blood tests
options.C: It guarantees that the patient will take all prescribed medications
options.D: It captures daily trends and avoids single-visit anxiety spikes

explanation: Ever get nervous seeing a doctor in a white coat? Wearables show real everyday trends without hospital stress getting in the way.

question: According to the Frank-Starling law, what happens when more blood returns to the heart?

options.A: The ventricles stretch more and pump out a stronger stroke volume
options.B: Myocardial oxygen consumption decreases significantly
options.C: The intercalated discs close tightly to prevent over-expansion
options.D: The heart rate drops immediately to allow more filling time

explanation: Think of the heart like a rubber band: the more it stretches as it fills with blood, the stronger it snaps back to pump that blood out!

question: After giving IV epinephrine, which vital signs must you monitor most closely?

options.A: Deep tendon reflex responses
options.B: Heart rate and blood pressure
options.C: Bowels sounds and abdominal tone
options.D: Peripheral capillary refill time

explanation: Spot on! Epinephrine is a powerful stimulant that makes the heart race and spikes blood pressure, so keeping a close eye on cardiovascular vitals is a must.

question: Which of the following is NOT a systemic risk associated with unsafe or unnecessary injections?

options.A: Systemic complications from contaminated equipment
options.B: Transmission of Hepatitis B and C viruses
options.C: Development of complete tolerance to oral painkillers
options.D: Acquisition of secondary bloodstream infections

explanation: Unsafe injections cause infections and bloodborne virus transmission, not oral drug tolerance. The question asks for what is NOT a risk. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h6)

question: When is the absolute best time for a patient to apply moisturizing creams (emollients)?

options.A: Once a week before going to sleep at night
options.B: Right before taking a hot shower to protect against the hot water
options.C: Only when the skin begins to crack and bleed visibly
options.D: Immediately after bathing while the skin is still slightly damp

explanation: You nailed it! Putting lotion on damp skin traps that wonderful moisture right inside where it belongs.

question: Before giving another dose of magnesium sulfate, which clinical sign must you check first?

options.A: Level of blood glucose
options.B: Size of the liver and spleen
options.C: Presence of knee-jerk patellar reflexes
options.D: Fetal heart rate variability

explanation: Awesome job! Losing the knee-jerk reflex is an early warning sign that magnesium is building up too much in the body, well before breathing slows down.

question: A nurse wants to test a new handwashing routine on two existing hospital wards without disrupting shift schedules. Which design fits best?

options.A: Quasi-experimental design
options.B: Historical research design
options.C: Phenomenological design
options.D: True experimental design

explanation: Spot on! When you have to use existing groups (like pre-formed wards) instead of mixing everyone randomly, you are doing a quasi-experiment.

question: What is the term used to describe the social, economic, and environmental factors that shape mental wellbeing?

options.A: Clinical diagnostic criteria
options.B: Biological stress markers
options.C: Social determinants of health
options.D: Hereditary personality traits

explanation: Social determinants of health encompass the conditions in which people are born, grow, live, work, and age that heavily influence mental health. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T7#GNS314_U1_T7_h2)

question: In antenatal care, what does BPCR stand for?

options.A: Baby Physical Care and Recovery
options.B: Birth Preparedness and Complication Readiness
options.C: Basic Physiological Childbirth Routine
options.D: Blood Pressure and Cardiac Response

explanation: You've got it! BPCR is all about helping families plan ahead for a normal delivery and know what to do if an emergency pops up.

question: What is the most common and preferred site for giving an intradermal injection?

options.A: Upper outer quadrant of the buttock
options.B: Volar surface of the forearm
options.C: Deltoid muscle of the upper arm
options.D: Anterior thigh muscle

explanation: Spot on! The inner forearm is easy to reach, has very little hair, and lets you clearly see any skin reactions.

question: About how many extra calories a day are needed in the later stages of pregnancy?

options.A: Three hundred calories
options.B: Two thousand calories
options.C: One thousand calories
options.D: Fifty calories

explanation: Spot on! An extra 300 calories a day—like a small, nourishing snack—is usually all it takes to fuel the final trimesters.

question: Knowing the exact classification and drug-resistance profile of an infecting organism directly helps the nurse do what?

options.A: Determining the patient's expected hospital discharge date
options.B: Administering targeted antimicrobial therapy effectively
options.C: Calculating the patient's exact daily fluid intake
options.D: Choosing the correct hospital room wall paint color

explanation: When you know the exact bug and what drugs it hates, the medical team can prescribe the precise medication to knock it out quickly and safely.

question: Why must sharps segregation happen immediately at the point of origin?

options.A: To make the sharps box heavier so it does not tip over
options.B: To comply with local fashion trends in hospital design
options.C: To prevent accidental needle-stick injuries during transport
options.D: To ensure the needles can be washed and reused later

explanation: Throwing needles directly into a nearby puncture-proof container stops nurses and cleaners from getting stuck while moving loose sharps later. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h4)

question: A patient asks for a safe way to cook potatoes on a low-fat diet. What should you suggest?

options.A: Baked or boiled without butter or sour cream
options.B: Pan-fried in rich bacon drippings for flavor
options.C: Deep-fried in vegetable oil until golden brown
options.D: Smashed with heavy whipping cream and whole milk

explanation: Exactly! Potatoes are naturally fat-free, but you must skip the added butter, cream, or oils.

question: Which of these is NOT a helpful medical or surgical option for managing tubal factor infertility?

options.A: Prolonged bed rest and pelvic massage
options.B: In Vitro Fertilization
options.C: Diagnostic and operative laparoscopy
options.D: Intrauterine insemination

explanation: Bed rest and massages cannot fix structural problems or short lengths in the fallopian tubes. Medical treatments like IVF or surgery are needed for that.

question: How do hydatid embryos first travel from the gut to organs like the liver?

options.A: Through the lymphatic drainage channels
options.B: Through the central nervous system pathways
options.C: By crawling directly through the abdominal wall
options.D: Through the portal venous system

explanation: After crossing the gut wall, they jump into blood vessels and ride the portal vein straight into the liver.

question: Which of these is an example of a structural heart problem that develops later in life (acquired)?

options.A: Tetralogy of Fallot malformation
options.B: Degenerative calcific aortic valve stenosis
options.C: Ventricular septal defect present at birth
options.D: Atrial septal defect from fetal development

explanation: Acquired conditions happen over time due to aging or wear and tear, unlike congenital defects that babies are born with. Great job working through this!

question: Which supplement is most important to give before pregnancy to help prevent birth defects?

options.A: Potassium chloride
options.B: Folic acid
options.C: Vitamin C
options.D: Calcium carbonate

explanation: Folic acid is a superstar vitamin! Taking it before and during early pregnancy greatly lowers the risk of neural tube defects like spina bifida. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h2)

question: When designing public health education, what does 'acceptability' mean?

options.A: Whether the target community welcomes and relates to the educational tool
options.B: Whether the government health ministry has stamped it with an official seal
options.C: How many pages of text the target population is willing to read
options.D: How cheaply the printing press can manufacture the paper flyers

explanation: Acceptability is all about whether the community feels comfortable with the material and feels it matches their personal values and beliefs.

question: What does a 'verbatim transcription' of a recorded interview mean?

options.A: Translating the interview into a foreign language
options.B: Converting audio files into exact written text word-for-word
options.C: Summarizing the main points into a single paragraph
options.D: Deleting all pauses and laughs from the recording

explanation: Spot on! Verbatim means capturing every single spoken word precisely as it was said to keep your research accurate.

question: What is the medical term for the complete absence of menstrual periods?

options.A: Menorrhagia
options.B: Dysmenorrhea
options.C: Amenorrhea
options.D: Metrorrhagia

explanation: Amenorrhea simply means 'no menses.' It can be primary (if periods never started) or secondary (if regular periods stopped).

question: Why is the family considered a primary unit of care in palliative care?

options.A: They are responsible for administering strong narcotics.
options.B: They pay the hospital bills directly out of pocket.
options.C: They experience the burden of illness and need support too.
options.D: They make all medical decisions without the patient.

explanation: Because a serious illness affects the entire family unit, palliative care extends support to relatives during the illness and through bereavement. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h2)

question: A patient with severe second-degree burns across their back requires which dietary adjustment?

options.A: High protein and high calorie intake to repair damaged skin tissues.
options.B: A strict clear liquid diet to rest the gastrointestinal tract.
options.C: Zero protein to keep the kidneys from working too hard.
options.D: Low calorie intake to prevent sudden weight gain during bed rest.

explanation: Burns cause massive protein loss and high metabolic stress, requiring extra protein and calories for wound healing and tissue regeneration. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T023#GNS227_U2_T023_h7)

question: Which lab result do you expect to see when a patient has acute endometritis?

options.A: High blood glucose level
options.B: Elevated white blood cell count
options.C: Decreased red blood cell count
options.D: Low platelet count

explanation: Since the body is fighting a bacterial invader, the bone marrow pumps out extra white blood cells, leading to a high white blood cell count on the lab report.

question: Where should you cough or sneeze if you don't have a tissue nearby?

options.A: Into your inner elbow or upper sleeve
options.B: Directly onto your clean uniform sleeve
options.C: Directly into the palm of your bare hand
options.D: Into the air away from other people

explanation: Brilliant! Coughing into your elbow keeps germs off your hands, preventing you from transferring them to door handles and patients.

question: What is a key nursing care action for a patient dealing with extreme fatigue from disseminated sclerosis?

options.A: Keeping the patient confined strictly to bed
options.B: Restricting all fluid intake after midday
options.C: Scheduling planned rest periods throughout the day
options.D: Encouraging intense daily marathon training

explanation: Pacing is everything! Balancing daily activities with scheduled rest helps patients conserve their energy without burning out.

question: What is a great community-level nursing action to help manage stress?

options.A: Closing down local markets to reduce neighborhood noise
options.B: Organizing mental health awareness campaigns and support groups
options.C: Prescribing strong antidepressant medications to every adult
options.D: Isolating stressed individuals inside regional hospitals

explanation: As community nurses, we shine brightest when we educate the public and create safe spaces where people can share and support one another.

question: Why do past surgeries in the tummy make a new laparoscopy trickier?

options.A: Dense scar tissue increases the risk of organ injury during entry
options.B: The patient will require a much higher dose of antibiotics
options.C: Carbon dioxide gas cannot be absorbed through scarred tissue
options.D: Special cameras are unable to function in scarred abdomens

explanation: You're learning fast! Old surgeries leave behind scar tissue (adhesions) that can pull intestines closer to the tummy wall, making it easier to accidentally nick them during instrument entry.

question: Which finding means the external ear canal is completely blocked?

options.A: A normal cone of light
options.B: Pars flaccida retraction
options.C: Cerumen impaction
options.D: An intact malleus bone

explanation: Cerumen impaction just means a buildup of earwax has packed tightly into the canal, blocking your view completely.

question: Why do clinics use the WHO staging system for HIV when lab tests for CD4 count are missing?

options.A: To guide clinical management using observable signs when CD4 counts are unavailable
options.B: To calculate the precise date when the patient was initially infected
options.C: To predict the exact genetic strain of the virus infecting the patient
options.D: To accurately measure the exact viral load circulating in the plasma

explanation: That's right! When lab equipment is scarce, checking physical signs and symptoms helps nurses and doctors choose the best care plan. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T2#GNS216_U6_T2_h5)

question: What do we call the tight, stiff, and involuntary muscle tone that often happens after a brain injury?

options.A: Contracture
options.B: Spasticity
options.C: Flaccidity
options.D: Atrophy

explanation: Spasticity is when muscles stay constantly contracted and stiff, making it tricky for the client to move or relax their limbs smoothly.

question: Why is pregnancy particularly tough on a teenage bride's physical body?

options.A: Her body is still growing and competes with the fetus for nutrients
options.B: Adult nutritional requirements no longer apply to her body
options.C: Her immune system completely shuts down during gestation
options.D: Hormonal changes stop her bones from ever healing properly

explanation: Teenagers are still growing themselves! Their bodies need nutrients for their own development, which creates a direct competition with the growing baby.

question: What happens when raw milk is left sitting at warm room temperature for too long?

options.A: Sugar content drops while protein content increases
options.B: The milk automatically undergoes safe pasteurization
options.C: Microorganisms multiply rapidly and cause spoilage
options.D: Natural antibiotics in the milk kill all bacteria

explanation: Spot on! Warmth plus all those rich nutrients means bacteria will multiply super fast, turning your fresh milk sour and curdled.

question: A patient asks why they need a special DEXA scan instead of a normal X-ray to check for weak bones. What is your best response?

options.A: Regular X-rays use too much radiation compared to modern bone density scanners
options.B: Standard X-rays cannot detect early bone loss until a large amount of mass is already gone
options.C: DEXA scans take pictures of soft muscle tissue rather than hard skeletal bone
options.D: Standard X-rays are only used for broken bones and cannot look at the spine

explanation: Regular X-rays are great for breaks, but they aren't sensitive enough to catch early osteoporosis. DEXA is specifically designed to measure tiny drops in bone strength.

question: What is a major risk of pushing a client too early into regular open employment?

options.A: Permanent immunity from all future mental health challenges
options.B: Sudden loss of physical mobility in the upper limbs

question: Which of these is a common informal support system in many Nigerian communities?

options.B: Extended family compounds and religious bodies

options.D: Government health insurance offices

question: What is the main purpose of conducting a hospital space audit?

options.A: To measure the exact weight of furniture located in administrative offices
options.B: To identify underutilized areas and evaluate how efficiently space is used
options.C: To determine the retail price of medical supplies sold to patients
options.D: To decide which clinical staff members deserve a salary increase

explanation: A space audit checks how rooms are actually being used so managers can make the most of current areas before deciding to build new extensions.

question: Beyond treating patients, what is an essential public health task for a nurse on an international disaster team?

options.A: Teaching community members about water purification and disease prevention
options.B: Auditing the international bank accounts of the United Nations
options.C: Negotiating ceasefire agreements between warring military factions
options.D: Purchasing international commercial airline tickets for arriving staff

explanation: Great job! Educating communities on hygiene and preventing disease outbreaks is just as vital as bedside nursing during a crisis.

question: What is the main goal of doing a statistical test on a research hypothesis?

options.A: To calculate the exact number of patients needed for a trial
options.B: To prove the null hypothesis is always correct
options.C: To see if there is enough evidence to reject the null hypothesis
options.D: To replace the alternative hypothesis with a descriptive chart

explanation: Spot on! We test our data to see if we have enough strong proof to throw out the null hypothesis and say our intervention actually works.

question: Why is it so important for the immune system to tell the difference between 'self' and 'non-self'?

options.A: It prevents the immune system from attacking healthy host tissues
options.B: It ensures that nutrients are absorbed properly in the intestines
options.C: It helps the body maintain a stable internal core temperature
options.D: It allows red blood cells to carry more oxygen to organs

explanation: Knowing what belongs to the body ('self') stops the immune system from mistakenly attacking healthy organs and tissues—which is what happens in autoimmune diseases!

question: What actually happens during an in-vitro fertilization (IVF) procedure?

options.A: Sperm are placed directly into the uterus using a small catheter
options.B: Blocked fallopian tubes are surgically tied and opened
options.C: Eggs and sperm are fertilized together in a laboratory dish
options.D: Hormone injections are given to stop natural ovulation

explanation: With IVF, eggs are collected, mixed with sperm in a lab dish to fertilize, and the resulting embryo is placed into the uterus.

question: What is the safest way to handle a used injection needle?

options.A: Break the needle off the syringe by hand
options.B: Drop it immediately into a puncture-resistant sharps container
options.C: Recap it firmly using both hands before walking away
options.D: Place it inside a regular plastic waste bin

explanation: You've got it! Never mess around with used needles. Drop them straight into the sharps box to avoid accidental pricks.

question: Which part of the nervous system takes over during non-REM sleep to slow your heart rate and lower blood pressure?

options.A: Sympathetic nervous system
options.B: Enteric nervous system
options.C: Somatic nervous system
options.D: Parasympathetic nervous system

explanation: The parasympathetic system is your 'rest and digest' mode. It slows things down so your body can conserve energy.

question: Which type of scale is best suited for an adult patient who is completely unable to stand?

options.A: A specialized chair or bed scale
options.B: A standard beam balance scale
options.C: A hanging infant spring scale
options.D: A flat digital floor scale

question: What is the main benefit of encouraging nurses to report 'near misses' in the clinic?

options.A: It allows managers to calculate exact salary deductions for staff
options.B: It gives the hospital legal protection against malpractice lawsuits
options.C: It fulfills mandatory federal tax reporting requirements
options.D: It helps the unit fix system flaws before a real patient injury happens

explanation: Near misses act like early warning signs, giving the team a chance to fix hidden dangers before a patient gets hurt.

question: In James Reason's famous Swiss cheese model of safety, what do the holes in the cheese represent?

options.A: The exact time a medication is due
options.B: Gaps in nursing school curriculum
options.C: The total number of patients admitted to a ward
options.D: Weaknesses in individual safety defense layers

explanation: Think of each cheese slice as a safety barrier. The holes are just the temporary cracks or flaws in those defenses.

question: Why do hospitals carefully sort and classify different types of medical waste?

options.A: It ensures all hospital refuse can be buried together safely
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for any protective personal equipment
options.C: It reduces the volume of general waste produced by patients
options.D: It dictates the correct treatment and disposal method for each item type

explanation: You've got this! Different waste types need specific treatments, like incineration for body parts or autoclaving for lab equipment. Sorting helps us do it safely.

question: What position should your patient be in when they drink fluids to prevent choking?

options.A: Upright at a 90-degree angle
options.B: Flat on their back in bed
options.C: Propped up at a 15-degree angle
options.D: Lying entirely on their left side

explanation: Gravity is your friend! Sitting upright helps guide liquids safely down the food pipe instead of heading toward the airway.

question: Why are healthy adults able to hold their urine even when their bladder feels quite full?

options.A: The external sphincter fuses shut until voluntary pressure is applied.
options.B: Sympathetic tone permanently paralyzes the detrusor muscle.
options.C: Higher brain centers send inhibitory signals that prevent the micturition reflex from executing.
options.D: The kidneys temporarily stop producing urine until a bathroom is found.

explanation: Your brain's higher centers have great self-control! They send downward messages to hold off the reflex until you actually reach a restroom.

question: What is the main way our normal body flora protects us from harmful invaders?

options.A: It directly attacks and destroys human immune cells for food
options.B: It produces high levels of stomach acid to kill parasites
options.C: It prevents harmful pathogens from finding space and nutrients to grow
options.D: It accelerates the digestion of complex proteins in the stomach

explanation: This is called microbial antagonism! Because our friendly bacteria already occupy all the good parking spots and eat the available food, nasty new germs can't easily find a place to move in.

question: At what exact point should healthcare waste be sorted into different bins?

options.A: Inside the municipal dumpsite before final burial
options.B: At the exact point of origin when the waste is generated
options.C: Late at night after all patients have gone to sleep
options.D: Only when the waste management officer arrives for inspection

explanation: Spot on! Sorting waste right at the bedside or clinic table stops mix-ups and keeps everyone safe.

question: A mother calls worried about a yellowish crust forming over her baby's healing circumcision. What is this?

options.A: Normal granulation tissue part of the healing process
options.B: Leftover residue from petroleum jelly ointment
options.C: A sign of a severe bacterial wound infection
options.D: Dried urine crystals from frequent wet diapers

explanation: No need to panic! That yellowish film is a normal part of how skin heals down there—reassure the mother it's not pus or an infection.

question: Which of these is a common biological reason for sexual dysfunction in older women?

options.A: Hyperactive thyroid function
options.B: Hormonal shifts during menopause
options.C: Excessive pelvic muscle tone
options.D: Increased production of estrogen

explanation: You've got it! Lower estrogen levels during menopause can cause dryness and tissue changes, which sometimes make things a bit uncomfortable.

question: How can nurses help solve scheduling problems caused by traditional family and caregiving duties?

options.A: By offering clinic hours that accommodate domestic responsibilities
options.B: By charging extra fees for patients who arrive late
options.C: By refusing to treat patients who have caregiving duties
options.D: By keeping clinics open only during standard morning work hours

explanation: Flexible clinic timings make it possible for people juggling heavy caregiving duties to still get the medical care they need. Wonderful thinking!

question: Unexplained facial hair growth in a female patient can be a sign of which condition?

options.A: Chronic kidney disease
options.B: Polycystic ovary syndrome
options.C: Iron deficiency anemia
options.D: Essential hypertension

explanation: Correct! Extra facial hair (hirsutism) is often linked to higher androgen levels, which are common in polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS).

question: What makes an interdisciplinary team different from a basic multidisciplinary team?

options.A: Interdisciplinary teams feature active communication and shared decision-making
options.B: Multidisciplinary teams always include community leaders and agriculture workers
options.C: Interdisciplinary teams restrict nurses from speaking during patient rounds
options.D: Multidisciplinary teams rely entirely on a single healthcare provider

explanation: Great thinking! While multidisciplinary teams work side-by-side, true interdisciplinary teams communicate closely and build care plans together.

question: Which pattern of knowing represents the science of nursing derived from research?

options.A: Empirical knowing
options.B: Ethical knowing
options.C: Aesthetic knowing
options.D: Personal knowing

explanation: Empirical knowing is your go-to science foundation—it relies on objective, observable data and actual research findings.

question: What is one of the first things a nurse should do regarding a patient's nutrition when they are admitted to the ward?

options.A: Prescribing specialized intravenous vitamin drips
options.B: Screening and monitoring the patient's dietary intake
options.C: Purchasing all grocery items from local markets
options.D: Performing surgical placement of feeding tubes

explanation: Checking what our patients eat right from admission helps us catch and stop hospital malnutrition early!

question: What is the main goal of Behavioural Change Communication (BCC) in public health?

options.A: Distributing medical supplies to rural clinics
options.B: Diagnosing rare tropical infectious diseases
options.C: Writing detailed hospital administration reports
options.D: Promoting positive and sustainable health habits

explanation: You've got this! BCC is all about using interactive ways to help people and communities build healthy habits that actually last.

question: What is the main job of carbohydrates in our daily diet?

options.A: Transporting fat-soluble vitamins through blood
options.B: Providing primary fuel for the brain and muscles
options.C: Building strong structural bone matrix
options.D: Synthesizing steroid reproductive hormones

explanation: Spot on! Carbs break down into glucose, which is your body's favorite energy source to keep you moving and studying all day long.

question: What is the main goal of rehabilitation nursing compared to regular hospital care?

options.A: Maximizing remaining abilities and independence
options.B: Strictly monitoring vital signs every hour
options.C: Curing the underlying pathological disease
options.D: Providing permanent total nursing dependence

explanation: While acute hospital care focuses on curing the disease, rehab is all about helping patients rebuild their strength and independence so they can live life to the fullest. You've got this!

question: Which embryonic tissue helps form your vertebrae and ribs as you develop?

options.A: Endodermal gut lining

options.D: Sclerotome cells from somites

question: Why is a CT scan with contrast usually preferred for a stable patient with suspected kidney trauma?

options.A: It uses zero radiation and requires no intravenous line placement.

options.C: It replaces the need to ever inspect the patient's urine for blood.

explanation: A contrast CT scan gives doctors a crystal-clear, detailed map showing if blood vessels are bleeding or if urine is leaking into the body. Super helpful tool!

question: Why is it important for psychiatric nurses to ask patients about alternative therapies?

options.A: Nurses are required to prescribe herbal remedies directly
options.B: Alternative therapies are always illegal in hospital settings
options.C: Patients frequently use them without telling their doctors
options.D: Standard psychiatric medications become completely useless

explanation: Many patients quietly take herbs or use local remedies without mentioning it. Asking them helps us keep them safe from bad drug reactions!

question: Which collaborative platform is most commonly integrated directly into secure hospital software systems?

options.A: Public social networks
options.B: Standard text messaging
options.C: Personal email accounts

question: When nurses talk about 'pathological waste', what are they referring to?

options.A: Used administrative office stationery

options.D: Empty medication boxes and paper files

question: What is the most important piece of advice to give a patient taking a 7-day course of antibiotics for cervicitis?

options.A: Share the remaining pills with your partner to save money.

options.C: Stop taking the pills immediately if mild stomach upset occurs.
options.D: Finish all the medication even if you start feeling better early.

explanation: Always remind patients to complete their full dose! Stopping early can cause the infection to bounce back stronger.

question: What is the main idea behind Charting by Exception (CBE)?

options.A: Only physicians are allowed to write progress notes
options.B: Only abnormal or unusual findings are documented
options.C: Documentation is done exclusively at the end of the week
options.D: Every single nursing action must be written in detail

explanation: CBE is a huge time-saver! It assumes everything is normal unless you write down a specific exception or problem.

question: Why is manually copying patient data dangerous in a clinical setting?

options.A: It automatically deletes vital sign history from the computer

options.C: It causes the hospital internet network to crash completely
options.D: It increases the risk of transcription errors and delays

question: What is the main goal of sex therapy when treating sexual dysfunction?

options.A: Treating underlying bacterial infections

options.D: Reducing performance anxiety and improving communication

question: What is the special component in fungal cell membranes that antifungal drugs love to target?

options.A: Cellulose
options.B: Peptidoglycan
options.C: Cholesterol

question: Why is malaria considered an endemic disease in Nigeria?

question: Why is accurate home care documentation especially critical compared to hospital notes?

options.A: Hospital records are destroyed as soon as the patient is discharged.

question: What goes on inside the body during the incubation period of an infection?

question: A patient with uncontrolled diabetes insists on a strict all-day fast. What is the major clinical risk to watch for?

options.A: Chronic deficiency of essential fatty acids
options.B: Rapid weight gain due to metabolic slowdown
options.C: Sudden accumulation of excess dietary calcium

question: What is the main job of Type A intercalated cells in the collecting duct?

question: What are the tiny, baby worms produced by adult Onchocerca volvulus called?

question: When you help a patient with their personal hygiene, why is it considered a special nursing care rather than just a normal house chore?

question: Which of these is NOT something educators look at when choosing your learning experiences?

question: Which theorist proposed that personality development happens across distinct psychosocial crises throughout the entire lifespan?

question: At what point in the hospital workflow should waste segregation take place?

question: When is chemical disinfection most commonly used in a healthcare facility?

options.B: For packaging expired patient food trays
options.C: For disposing of heavy metal surgical instruments
options.D: For processing large wooden crates and office furniture

question: What turns a natural hazard like a flood into a disaster?

options.A: When international media reports on it

options.D: When rainfall exceeds historical averages

question: What usually happens when a clinical unit experiences chronic understaffing?

question: Which bloodborne viruses are most commonly transmitted through unsafe injection practices?

question: Which bacteria is most commonly linked to undercooked poultry and eggs?

question: Why are peer educators so helpful in community health outreach?

question: What do we mean by 'self-tolerance' in the immune system?

options.A: How fast white blood cells multiply during an infection

options.C: Making antibodies against common foods
options.D: The ability to recognize and ignore the body's own healthy tissues

question: What do macroeconomic indicators provide for a country?

question: An asthmatic patient starts wheezing and coughing after spending the afternoon outside on a heavy smog day. What caused this attack?

options.C: A sudden bacterial invasion of the bloodstream
options.D: Complete destruction of the heart valves due to low oxygen

explanation: Correct! Smog irritates sensitive airways, making the muscles around them tighten up and swell, which triggers asthma symptoms.

question: Why are the tiny blood vessels (capillaries) inside endocrine glands specially built?

question: What is the first thing a birth attendant should check on a delivery kit before opening it?

question: How do patient satisfaction surveys help a home health agency improve its care?

explanation: Listening directly to client feedback gives agencies clear insight into what's working and where care can be made even better.

question: What is the primary job of the Leydig cells found in the testes?

options.A: To store mature sperm cells

options.D: To nourish the urinary bladder

question: A nurse manager notices constant bickering among staff over shift rosters and fairness. What is the best proactive step to take?

question: What is a major challenge that family caregivers often face when looking after a sick relative at home?

question: What is the main difference between sampling error and sampling bias?

options.A: Sampling error only happens in qualitative studies, while bias happens in quantitative studies

question: Why is it important to ensure that traction weights hang freely off the bed?

question: What is a major risk if a woman hyperventilates too severely during the second stage of labour?

question: Why is teamwork between different healthcare pros so important in home nutrition care?
